item.title: 奥普拉·温弗瑞表示她明年将关闭南非的女子学校
item.description:
约翰内斯堡（美联社）——奥普拉·温弗瑞表示，她将在明年年底关闭她二十年前在南非为贫困女孩设立的学校。
受到与南非前总统纳尔逊·曼德拉关于教育女孩的变革力量的对话的启发，温弗瑞于 2007 年开设了奥普拉·温弗瑞女子领导力学院。他是学校开幕式的嘉宾之一。
该学院表示，温弗瑞的慈善基金会负责运营并资助这所学校，但约翰内斯堡附近的学院校园最终移交给省教育部门始终是协议的一部分。
“梦想从来不仅仅是建造一所学校，”温弗瑞在学院周三发布的一份声明中表示。“这是为了投资年轻女性的无限潜力。这一使命并不仅仅限于一个校园。它继续存在于每一个可以通过教育改变未来的女孩身上。”
该学院表示，温弗瑞将通过扩大国家奖学金计划继续致力于教育南非女孩，以支持全国领先学校中具有学术才华的女孩。
据奥普拉·温弗瑞慈善基金会称，已有 500 多名女孩从该学院毕业，其中一些女孩进入了南非、美国和欧洲的顶尖大学。
豪登省政府将接管占地 52 英亩的学院校园，该校园设有 21 间教室、6 个科学和计算机实验室、一个藏书 10,000 册的图书馆和一个 600 个座位的剧院。它没有立即透露该房产的计划是什么。
豪登省教育部长Lebogang Maile表示，目前在学校就读的学生将能够在不间断的财政支持下完成学业。
该学院于 2007 年开学后不久就引起了国际关注，当时几名学生指控一名宿舍管理员对他们进行身体虐待和性虐待。
温弗瑞前往南非会见学生和家长，公开道歉，并委托进行独立调查。
2010年，这位女护士的刑事指控被无罪释放。
该报告已更正，以显示奥普拉·温弗瑞周三而非周四发表的声明。

item.title: 白宫暗示特朗普正在考虑对伊朗和中东其他事态发展进行新的打击
item.description:
CAIRO (AP) — The White House on Friday signaled that PresidentDonald Trumpis weighing carrying out new strikes on Iran as the U.S. presses for Tehran to reopen theStrait of Hormuzand abide by terms set out in a truce agreement the two sides forged last month only to quickly collapse.
There were no U.S. strikes on Iran overnight, but Iran’s paramilitary Revolutionary Guard said it hadstruck another two tankersin theStrait of Hormuz, and Kuwait said it intercepted drones.
Meanwhile, Hamas confirmed Friday thatit will disarmin a potential breakthrough for ending the war in Gaza, but major obstacles remain.
Here are the most important developments across the Middle East today:
White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt expressed the U.S. administration’s frustration anew, charging that Tehran last month signed a memorandum of understanding with the U.S. on a truce but then quickly “broke it, shot at commercial ships, and killed American soldiers.”
“President Trump is not going to stand by and allow this terrorist behavior to occur,” Leavitt said in a statement on Friday evening. “Iran will continue to pay until they come to the table in, what President Trump deems, a meaningful way.”
Leavitt issued the fresh warning after Trump earlier on Friday told reporters that “we just want to win” in Iran and signaled that he expected U.S. military action to continue for some time.
“We’ll be hitting them very hard,” Trump said in an exchange with reporters during a meeting with members of his Cabinet at the Camp David presidential retreat in Maryland. “You know, at some point they’re going to say, ‘We just can’t take it anymore.’”
Iran fired drones at Kuwait, a Gulf country hosting U.S. forces, and said it had also fired at oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, a key waterway for global oil and gas shipments, which has been largely closed by the fighting.
Kuwait’s Defense Ministry said Friday its armed forces had shot down drones inside Kuwaiti airspace. It said the Iranian attacks had targeted several vital military facilities, causing material damage from falling shrapnel but no casualties. It did not specify how many drones were intercepted. Iranian state media said Iran had targeted an air base in Kuwait with drones in retaliation for U.S. strikes on Thursday.
Iran’s Revolutionary Guard claimed to have hit two oil tankers attempting to pass through the Strait of Hormuz. Iranian state media said four other tankers had turned around. The report did not provide further details on the tankers’ ownership, or whether there were any casualties.
Hamas said it will begin disarming as part of a deal announced by Trump that also requires Israel to end its strikes and withdraw from Gaza.
Hamas also said that laying down its heavy weapons, which would come later in the process, was contingent on the creation of a Palestinian state, something Israel’s current government adamantly rejects.
Reflecting the hurdles of the potential disarmament, a series of Israeli airstrikes shook Gaza again on Friday, killing at least one Palestinian and wounding at least four, including a child, according to officials in hospitals near the attacks. The Israeli military did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres welcomed the agreement, calling it the only good news in recent days from a troubled region. The deal must be implemented “without any questions, skepticism, or determination to undermine it,” he told reporters.
Israel has not officially commented on the Hamas deal, which is part of aU.S.-brokered ceasefireannounced last October. That agreement called for Hamas to disarm and hand over power to an independent Palestinian administration. Israel was to withdraw and anInternational Stabilization Forcewas to be deployed.
But progress stalled, with Israel saying everything hinged on Hamas disarming, and Hamas accusing Israel of violating the agreement by continuing to carry out regular strikes on Gaza.
The war in Gaza began after the Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on Oct. 7, 2023, killed around 1,200 people and saw 251 taken hostage. Israel’s retaliatory offensive in Gaza has killed more than 73,000 Palestinians, including those killed since the ceasefire, Gaza’s Health Ministry says.
The Associated Pressis tracking the progressof Trump’s plan to end the Israel-Hamas war.
1. Saudi Arabia has announced a plan for a defense alliance of 14 countries to strengthen maritime security, safeguard freedom of navigation and secure international trade routes and energy supply corridors in the Red Sea region. The Iran war has severely disrupted global shipping. Yemen’s Houthi rebels have declared a blockade on Saudi Arabia over a separate but related conflict, putting at riskanother major trade corridor.
2. Saudi Arabia’s Defense Ministry said Thursday that the coalition is “defensive in nature,” and that access “remains open to all willing countries.” Oman and the United Arab Emirates were the only two Gulf countries that did not back Saudi Arabia’s statement. Turkey, Egypt and Pakistan were among those that joined the proposed alliance.
3. A Houthi official, speaking Friday on condition of anonymity because he wasn’t authorized to brief the media, said the Saudi initiative won’t protect its vessels — that would happen only after the Saudis lift their blockade on Yemen. Large crowds of Yemenis, meanwhile, took to the streets in the capital, Sanaa, and other Houthi-controlled areas to show support for the Iran-backed rebels and their Red Sea attacks against Saudi Arabia. The rallies were organized by the Houthis.
4. In southern Lebanon, Israeli forces set off explosions Friday to destroy an underground tunnel network under the Crusader-built Beaufort Castle that Israel says had been used by Hezbollah militants as a command center. The 12th-century castle, also known as Al-Shaqif, was seized by Israeli forces in May. It was recently added to UNESCO’s World Heritage List over Israel’s objections.
5. Lebanon’s President Joseph Aoun said the Israeli operation sent “negative messages” ahead of upcoming talks in Rome. Israeli and Lebanese negotiating teams are set to meet again there to continue hammering out a plan under which Israel would withdraw from southern Lebanon in exchange for Hezbollah’s disarmament.
Madhani reported from Washington and Becatoros contributed from Athens, Greece. Associated Press writer Fatma Khaled contributed to this report from Cairo.

item.title: 多瑙河水位创历史新低，匈牙利准备全面关闭帕克斯核电站
item.description:
匈牙利布达佩斯（美联社）——匈牙利总理彼得·马扎尔周五表示，由于多瑙河水位创历史新低，匈牙利唯一的核电站将在其历史上首次关闭，并补充说，由于预计河流水位将继续退缩，该核电站可能在几周内不会恢复运行。
Paks 核电站位于首都布达佩斯以南约 90 公里（50 英里）处，目前的运行能力还不到正常容量的一半，发电量为 965 兆瓦，而不是通常的 2,000 兆瓦。
该工厂使用多瑙河的水来冷却其反应堆，但极低的水位考验了水泵将足够水量输送到工厂的能力。
马扎尔周五在工厂举行的新闻发布会上表示，周五晚些时候即将进一步减产，整个工厂可能会在周二或周三关闭。他强调，关闭可以安全进行，不会对公众或环境构成风险。
苏联在帕克斯建造的四反应堆发电厂占匈牙利电力生产的近一半。如果它断电，这将是其服役 44 年来的第一次。
近几个月来，匈牙利和中欧大部分地区经历了长期干旱，扰乱了旅游业、农业和工业，并使居民面临气候变化的现实。由于预计不会有大量降雨，预计未来几天甚至几周内多瑙河水位不会上升。
Magyar周五表示，过去20年多瑙河水位仅在8月份上涨过3次，并补充说，帕克斯的水位可能会回落至负144厘米（负57英寸），远低于2018年创下的负98厘米（负39英寸）的纪录。
他说，如果水位达到负 134 厘米，就需要工厂完全断电。负读数意味着河流已降至仪表的零参考水位以下，而不是河流已空。
匈牙利政府已要求消耗大量能源的大公司自愿减少消耗，以帮助稳定能源供应，特别是在下午5点至下午5点之间的需求高峰时段。晚上 10 点
Magyar表示，匈牙利能源集团MOL已承诺将电力需求减少65兆瓦时，比正常消耗量减少40%。
马扎尔周五宣布，他的政党建议暂停原定于周一和周二举行的议会会议，以节省能源。他还下令所有国家机构在周一之前关闭装饰照明。

item.title: 当局在南希·格思里 (Nancy Guthrie) 案件中提前发布了赎金字条，希望有人认出它
item.description:
PHOENIX (AP) — Authorities released an early ransom note in the investigation into thedisappearance of Nancy Guthriein hopes that someone will recognize the writing style. A second note, also released Friday, said Guthrie died shortly after she was kidnapped and “is buried in nature now.”
Both notes initially were sent to a Tucson television station days after the 84-year-old mother of“Today” show host Savannah Guthriewent missing from her home outside Tucson on Feb. 1. Authorities have not said whether Nancy Guthrie is still alive.
Saturday is the six-month mark since Guthrie went missing. No suspects have been arrested in her disappearance. The investigation is dogged by unanswered questions, such as how many people are believed to have taken part in her abduction and whether she was taken by someone who knew her.
In her latestvideoabout her mother’s disappearance, Savannah Guthrie said earlier this week that her family has been living an unending nightmare and pleaded with the kidnappers to “tell us where to look for her.”
The FBI in Washington did not immediately respond to questions about the ransom notes, including whether both messages sent to the Tucson station have been deemed legitimate.
In releasing the notes, the Pima County Sheriff’s Department said “we believe these distinctive linguistic characteristics may be recognizable to someone who knows or has interacted with the notes’ writer.”
Thefirst note, sent Feb. 2, said Guthrie was safe but scared and would be released unharmed once her captors received $4 million in cryptocurrency, with the ransom amount increasing if the first demand was not met.
It said Guthrie would be released within 12 hours if the payment was received. It also included a threat to kill her if the ransom wasn’t paid.
“Your mother is aware of this and her life is in your hands,” the first note read. “It is in the best interest of everyone to have this completed as soon as possible.”
Thesecond notewas sent Feb. 6 and said Guthrie died shortly after she was taken. “She is buried in nature now,” it said. “Nothing you could have done could have changed the outcome.” The note ended with an apology: “We are truly sorry.”
A collection of yellow flowers and notes sit at the home of Nancy Guthrie, the missing mother of “Today” show host Savannah Guthrie, in Tucson, Ariz., March 6, 2026. (AP Photo/Rebecca Noble, File)
The sheriff’s department said the notes reveal a distinctive pattern of word choices and provide insight into the writer’s mindset. The agency said someone who knows the notes’ writer may recognize the patterns.
Authorities similarly used a suspect’s own writings as a tool to apprehendTheodore “Ted” Kaczynski, branded the “Unabomber” by the FBI. Kaczynski, who killed three people and injured 23 others with mail bombs over a 17-year span, pressured The Washington Post, in conjunction with The New York Times, to publish his 35,000-word manifesto in 1995. Federal authorities encouraged its publication, leading Kaczynski’s brother and sister-in-law to recognize the syntax and anti-technology themes and tip off the FBI, bringing to a close the agency’s longest and costliest investigation at the time.
In a statement Friday, the sheriff’s department also appealed to people who may know something about the case, saying it may be difficult to come forward due to a personal relationship with someone involved or just for their own safety.
“We recognize relationships and loyalties change over time as do people and their perspectives,” the sheriff’s department wrote. “It is not too late to come forward.”
The sheriff’s office also said Friday that two videos recovered from Guthrie’s doorbell camera might be from two separate days and indicate an unidentified male prepared ahead of when Guthrie was taken. Authorities are seeking information on anyone who was behaving differently, changed their physical appearance, suddenly left the Tucson area, or had a noticeable or unexplained interest or disinterest in the case.
“Investigators continue to pursue every available technological and investigative lead,” the sheriff’s office said. “However, community members remain a vital resource as we seek to provide answers for Nancy’s family.”
People visit a banner for Nancy Guthrie, the missing mother of “Today” show host Savannah Guthrie, outside the KVOA Newsroom in Tucson, Ariz., on March 6, 2026. (AP Photo/Rebecca Noble, File)
The FBI had released surveillance videos of a masked person who authorities said appeared to tamper with a camera on Nancy Guthrie’s front porch and block it with a plant. They described the person as a male about 5 feet, 9 inches (1.75 meters) tall.
On Feb. 4, Savannah Guthrie and her siblings first shared avideo statementsaying they were aware of media reports of a purported ransom letter and that they were ready to talk and listen, but they wanted proof that their mother was alive. Camron Guthrie, the brother of the “Today” co-anchor, said the following day that the familyhad not heard directlyfrom whoever took their mother.
A day after the second note was sent, Savannah Guthrie said on Feb. 7 that the siblings received a message and “understand,” without sharing details. She said they were begging for their mother to be returned to them. “We will pay,” Guthrie said.
The family has continued to share their pleas for information in videos posted to social media.
Also, two men detained and released early in the investigation into Nancy Guthrie’s disappearance are seeking a combined $3 million against a southern Arizona sheriff’s department. In a legal claim, they say they were wrongfully held by law enforcement.
The claim made Thursday against Pima County Sheriff Chris Nanos’ department centers on the separate detentions of Carlos Alfredo Palazuelos and Daniel Maddow on Feb. 10. It said they were released hours later but have suffered from having been mentioned in the investigation.
Nanos’ office declined to comment on the notice of claim, a necessary precursor to filing a lawsuit against government entities.
Associated Press writer Hannah Schoenbaum in Salt Lake City contributed.

item.title: 海军陆战队称F-35B隐形战斗机在加州坠毁，飞行员安全弹射
item.description:
圣迭戈（美联社）——美国海军陆战队表示，一架 F-35B 隐形战斗机的飞行员在加州坠毁前从飞机上弹射，预计能生还。
这架飞机周五在圣地亚哥米拉马尔空军基地附近坠毁。海军陆战队在一份最新声明中表示：“飞行员弹射逃生，被送往当地一家医疗机构，情况稳定，接受评估和治疗，伤势不危及生命。”
一架新闻直升机的航拍视频显示，泥土地里的残骸中升起一股黑烟，附近有多辆军用和消防车辆以及人员。地面上覆盖着白色阻燃剂，至少有一个人正在用消防水带向残骸喷洒。
韦德·洛特 (Wade Lott) 开车前往位于航线以南的一家混凝土公司上班时目睹了这起坠机事件。
“它刚刚爆炸了，太疯狂了，”36 岁的洛特说，他在卡车上看着两架喷气式飞机一起降落到跑道上。洛特说，第一架飞机着陆时没有发生任何事故，但第二架飞机突然开始减速，几乎就像试图悬停一样。当喷气式飞机距地面约 100 英尺（30 m）时，飞行员及时弹射，降落伞展开，升到空中约 200 英尺（61 m）。
“这架喷气式飞机就在另一架飞机旁边撞上了地面，”洛特说。“它冲进跑道然后爆炸了。”
圣地亚哥消防局发言人坎迪斯·哈德利表示，消防员正在现场应对坠机现场附近引发的植被火灾。她向海军陆战队米拉马尔航空站提出了其他问题。
该基地曾是电影《壮志凌云》中描绘的海军战斗机飞行员训练学校的所在地，全盛时期被称为“美国战斗机城”。1996年，该基地移交给海军陆战队后，学校搬迁至内华达州法伦海军航空站。
根据美国政府会计办公室 2024 年的分析，美国海军陆战队、海军和空军总共拥有 630 多架 F-35。F-35B 是多个版本之一，拥有专为短距起飞和垂直着陆而设计的发动机。一架 F-35B 的造价约为 1.09 亿美元。该报告估计，在军方购买超过 1,800 架喷气式飞机并在未来几十年内运行后，整个 F-35 项目将花费约 2 万亿美元。
海军陆战队的一份声明称周五的坠机事件为“A 级事故”。这是最严重的事故类别，当损失总额超过 200 万美元、飞机被毁或军人死亡时使用。根据空军安全中心的统计，自 2000 年以来，仅在空军中，就至少发生了 17 起涉及 F-35 飞机的其他“A 级事故”。
根据飞行安全基金会的航空安全网络数据库，今年美国还至少发生了七起军用飞机事故。
根据专注于国防技术和国家安全的列克星敦研究所智囊团的说法，F-35 被认为是军方机队中最安全、最强大的战斗机。
自 2015 年采用 F-35 以来，与其他战斗机刚推出时相比，涉及任何 F-35 型号的坠机事故都较少，而且 F-35 发生致命坠机事故的情况也很少。
在 F-35 的五次坠机事故中，飞行员均成功弹射，但至少有一名飞行员受伤。2024 年 5 月，一架 F-35 在新墨西哥州阿尔伯克基国际机场附近坠毁，该飞行员受伤。这架飞机当时正从德克萨斯州飞往加利福尼亚州的一个空军基地。
美联社交通部撰稿人乔什·芬克 (Josh Funk) 在内布拉斯加州奥马哈对本报告做出了贡献。丽贝卡·布恩 (Rebecca Boone) 来自爱达荷州博伊西。

item.title: Justice Department moves to drop case against ex-Olympian charged with damaging Reflecting Pool
item.description:
华盛顿（美联社）——周五，司法部驳回了一项指控一名前奥运选手故意破坏林肯纪念堂倒影池的刑事案件，称检察官最近收到的证据驳斥了破坏行为是罪魁祸首的观点。
政府律师在一份长达 20 页的法庭文件中表示，自大卫·赫恩 (David Hearn) 被起诉以来，内政部提供的更多文件显示，造成损坏的原因是承包商安装不当，以及“在 2026 年独立日前后几周的美国 250 周年庆祝活动之前急于完成该项目”。此外，最近的目视检查显示整个泳池都受到了损坏，包括中间的地方——检察官表示，破坏者不太可能试图剥掉泳池的内衬。
美国检察官珍妮·皮罗 (Jeanine Pirro) 在提交的文件中表示：“鉴于所有这些新发现的信息，很难将倒影池的广泛损坏归咎于故意破坏行为，更不用说在合理怀疑范围内证实这一事实。”该文件要求法官正式驳回此案。
赫恩的律师在一份声明中表示，根本不应该对他提起诉讼。
“今天的驳回并不能消除滥用政府权力逮捕和指控一名没有做错的爱国美国人的行为。政府的做法已经准备好了，开火，瞄准。政府欠赫恩先生道歉，”律师们说。
这次解雇对司法部来说是一个尴尬的挫折，司法部曾指责检方对华盛顿地标建筑造成的损害负责，唐纳德·特朗普总统在美国建国 250 周年庆典之前启动了一项大规模翻修工程。特朗普在没有提供证据的情况下声称损坏是由破坏行为造成的。
但该案长期以来一直面临证据问题和挑战。数周以来，赫恩一直坚称自己无罪，他的支持者将此次起诉定性为特朗普政府出于政治动机试图转移责任并寻找替罪羊。
本周早些时候，赫恩的律师寻求查阅大陪审团的笔录，因为他们称这一过程存在“违规行为”。他们说，国家公园管理局的一名官员作证说，在赫恩涉嫌触碰泳池之前，该泳池就已经遭到损坏，无法量化赫恩造成的任何损坏，并表示无论他的行为如何，都需要进行相同的维修。
“证人的证词证实，在赫恩先生做出任何指控的行为之前，泳池已经存在严重损坏，需要修复，”他的律师写道。“据目击者称，泳池每周泄漏的水超过一百万加仑；其伸缩缝已超过使用寿命；内衬已出现裂口。”
赫恩本月早些时候对一项破坏财产重罪表示不认罪，并计划于 9 月 28 日在华盛顿特区高等法院开始审判。该指控指控赫恩对泳池造成至少 1,000 美元的损失，一旦定罪，最高可判处 10 年监禁。
在周五的法庭文件中，检察官表示，他们最近才收到破坏起诉依据的新信息。
“直到这些文件出示后，（检察官）才第一次意识到有信息表明，损坏是由于安装不当造成的，而不是内政部最初所代表的破坏行为。”他们写道，检察官“只能依赖”表明损坏是由破坏行为造成的初步信息。
赫恩告诉美联社，6 月 19 日，他在骑自行车时停在泳池边，之后被国民警卫队和美国公园警察拘留了五个小时。他说，他伸手检查泳池新剥落的涂层，并短暂触摸了附着在泳池一侧的一块块，但他说，他服从了一名公园工作人员的要求，让他放开它。
美国奥林匹克和残奥委员会在其网站上称，67 岁的赫恩来自马里兰州贝塞斯达，参加了三届夏季奥运会，并在 1996 年亚特兰大奥运会上获得了第九名。

item.title: 特朗普称国税局和解中的反武器化基金已“死亡”，尽管他为其辩护
item.description:
WASHINGTON (AP) — President Donald Trump said Friday that his$1.8 billion anti-weaponization fundis “dead” while also continuing to defend it, further complicating his administration’s negotiations with two Republican senators who are blocking hisattorney general nomineein protest.
Trump told reporters at Camp David on Friday morning that administration officials had “agreed not to have a fund” that compensates his political allies, yet made clear that he disagrees with that decision.
The comments came hours after an early morning social media post in which Trump said people who had been prosecuted by the Justice Department — many of them for theirinvolvement in the violent Jan. 6, 2021, attack on the Capitol— “are suffering still, many ruined, and I felt that they should be given compensation for what has been done to them.”
Trump’s reluctant declaration that the fund won’t be created came as Republican Sens. John Cornyn of Texas and Thom Tillis of North Carolina, both members of the Senate Judiciary Committee, say they won’t support Todd Blanche’s nomination for attorney general until they see that promise in writing. They have been working for weeks with the White House and Blanche, who is now the acting attorney general, to produce a document to that effect, but both senators have said they aren’t satisfied so far.
“The President made it clear today that the so-called Anti Weaponization Fund is still alive, which is exactly why we are attempting to formally end it,” Tillis said after Trump’s initial social media post.
As negotiations continued late Friday, Senate Judiciary Committee Chairman Chuck Grassley rescheduled a committee vote for Blanche that had been postponed earlier in the week.
A spokesperson for the committee said Grassley would like to see Blanche confirmed before the August recess and putting the Tuesday vote on the calendar “gives more time for the White House to secure the votes for the President’s nominee.”
Blanche said at a hearing two months ago that the anti-weaponization fund would not move forward after Republican senators revolted and held up an immigration funding bill.
But Tillis, who isretiringwhen his term ends in January, and Cornyn, wholost reelectionthis year after Trump endorsed his primary opponent, said they want to ensure that the White House doesn’t reverse course, especially as Trump continues to argue that a fund is needed.
The Justice Department has provided the senators with language that says Blanche’s May 18 order establishing the “Anti-Weaponization Fund” is “rescinded and shall have no force or effect,” according to a document reviewed by The Associated Press.
Cornyn and Tillis have said they also want some clarifications on a separate piece of the settlement that would grant Trump and members of his family immunity from tax audits. Cornyn said this week that it was his understanding that the audits could extend to more than 100 different Trump organization subsidiaries into the future.
“Todd Blanche said it was limited to the parties to the litigation — and it was retrospective, not prospective,” Cornyn said. “And all we’re doing is asking them to put that in writing.”
The Judiciary Committeepostponed the vote on Blanche’s nominationthat had been scheduled for Thursday morning after Tillis and Cornyn said they needed more from the administration before they could provide the necessary votes.
After the meeting was delayed, Trump said in a social media post thathe might pull Blanche’s nominationand resubmit it after Cornyn and Tillis leave office next year. But the two sides continued to negotiate through Thursday afternoon, when Blanche, Cornyn and Tillis met on Capitol Hill.
On Friday, a person familiar with the negotiations said talks had been positive but the senators were still awaiting a new offer from the Justice Department. The person requested anonymity to discuss the private negotiations.
The two senators have repeatedly said the Justice Department seemed interested in reaching an agreement, but the White House wouldn’t budge even to aid the confirmation of Trump’s loyal former personal attorney, who hasaggressively pursued the administration’s prioritiesas acting attorney general.
“I think as far as Blanche and the Department of Justice, we were pretty much on the same page,” Cornyn said Thursday. “But then when the president got wind of it, he wasn’t willing to go along with it.”
Tillis said Blanche “has been forthright, thoughtful and patient” but attributed the holdup to an “incompetent personal adviser” to the president, even as Trump himself continued to advocate for the fund.
Behind the scenes, Trump legal adviser Boris Epshteyn is being blamed as an obstacle to an agreement that would let Blanche move forward, according to three people who have direct knowledge of the discussions and requested anonymity to discuss them.
Saying the AP’s “sources are wrong,” White House communications director Steven Cheung said “anyone trying to assign blame to the President or his team has no earthly idea of what is going on and clearly is trying to deflect from the issue at hand — Todd Blanche will be an exceptional Attorney General and he should be confirmed immediately.”
Also on Friday, Trump’s attorneys notified a court it would appeal a judge’s scathing ruling that characterized the settlement of the president’s lawsuit against the IRS as animproper exercise in self-dealing.The judge in her order earlier this month referred one of Trump’s attorneys for potential disciplinary action and criticized Blanche’s involvement in the settlement, given his prior representation of Trump.
Blanche has said he disagrees “with the judge’s insinuations” about him.
Even as they are usually deferential to Trump, a number of Republican senators have expressed strong objections to the settlement.
“The criminals who assaulted police officers and defiled our nation’s Capitol are not ‘great American patriots’ who are ‘victims of government abuse,’” Tillis said, echoing Trump’s comments about the rioters who could potentially have received payouts. On his first day back in office, Trump pardoned more than 1,500 people who had been charged in the attack.
Republican Sen. John Kennedy of Louisiana said Thursday that the majority of Senate Republicans aren’t comfortable with the settlement fund.
“Blanche said it’s dead, and he testified that it’s not coming back,” Kennedy said. “But for whatever reason, somebody didn’t want to put it in writing.”
This story has been updated to correct the year of the Capitol riot. It was 2021, not 2001.
Associated Press writers Eric Tucker and Lisa Mascaro contributed to this report.

item.title: 多年来，戴维营是总统在马里兰州乡村的山区度假胜地
item.description:
华盛顿（美联社）——周五，唐纳德·特朗普总统离开金色的白宫，前往马里兰州山区质朴的戴维营参加内阁会议。
该静修处位于华盛顿西北约一小时车程处，自富兰克林·罗斯福在二战期间建立此静修处以来，这里一直是总统峰会和小规模会议的举办地。周五的会议并不是特朗普第一次在戴维营举行，但他在戴维营待的时间比其他总统要少，而且通常会在自己的地产上度过周末，包括佛罗里达州棕榈滩的海湖庄园以及他在新泽西州和弗吉尼亚州的高尔夫球场。
以下是集中营历史上的一些关键日期和著名访客，这些都是使用美联社、国家档案馆和总统图书馆的档案材料整理而成的。
1942 年——罗斯福将营地命名为“香格里拉”，灵感源自詹姆斯·希尔顿的小说《消失的地平线》。罗斯福喜欢在总统游艇上放松，但第二次世界大战期间，军方和特勤局开始担心他在开放水域的安全。罗斯福要求国家公园管理局在白宫 100 英里范围内寻找可供他休息的地点，并选择了现在被称为戴维营的地点。
1943 年 — 罗斯福接待了温斯顿·丘吉尔，丘吉尔与总统一起去钓鱼，并在度假胜地讨论了诺曼底登陆问题。
1953 年 — 德怀特·艾森豪威尔 (Dwight Eisenhower) 以他的孙子和父亲的名字将该设施重新命名为戴维营。
1961 年 4 月 22 日，约翰·肯尼迪总统和前总统德怀特·艾森豪威尔在马里兰州瑟蒙特附近的山顶戴维营讨论古巴危机后，沿着石板路行走，步伐完美。背景是营地的一间小屋。（美联社照片，文件）
1959 年——艾森豪威尔接待了尼基塔·赫鲁晓夫，这是苏联领导人首次访问美国。
1971 年——在通货膨胀和黄金挤兑迫在眉睫的情况下，理查德·尼克松 (Richard Nixon) 会见了经济顾问，最终宣布结束黄金支持的美元。
1973 年——尼克松接待了苏联总统勃列日涅夫。
1978 年 — 吉米·卡特接待了埃及的安瓦尔·萨达特和以色列的梅纳赫姆·贝京，最终于 1979 年签署了《戴维营协议》。与记者进进出出的白宫不同，新闻媒体被禁止进入戴维营，除非他们被邀请报道某个活动，例如周五的峰会。
1984年——在戴维营停留时间最长的总统罗纳德·里根首次接待了英国首相玛格丽特·撒切尔。
在这张 1981 年 7 月白宫发布的档案照片中，美国总统罗纳德·里根（左）和副总统乔治·布什在马里兰州戴维营骑马（迈克尔·埃文斯/白宫，来自美联社，档案）
1990 — 乔治·H.W.布什接待了苏联领导人米哈伊尔·戈尔巴乔夫。
1992 年——戴维营唯一的一场婚礼是布什的女儿多萝西 (Dorothy) 在该设施的长青教堂 (Evergreen Chapel) 与鲍比·科赫 (Bobby Koch) 结婚。
2000年——比尔·克林顿与以色列总理埃胡德·巴拉克和巴勒斯坦权力机构主席亚西尔·阿拉法特主持峰会。
2000 年 7 月 11 日星期二，中东峰会开始时，比尔·克林顿总统、以色列总理埃胡德·巴拉克（左）和巴勒斯坦领导人亚西尔·阿拉法特（右）在马里兰州戴维营的场地上行走。（美联社照片/罗恩·埃德蒙兹，档案）
2001 年——乔治·W·布什 (George W. Bush) 于年初会见了英国首相托尼·布莱尔 (Tony Blair)，并在当年晚些时候入侵阿富汗之前举行了 9/11 事件后的会议。
2007 年 8 月 6 日星期一，乔治·W·布什总统（左）在阿富汗总统哈米德·卡尔扎伊（右）的陪同下，在马里兰州戴维营举行的联合新闻发布会上做出手势（美联社照片/J. Scott Applewhite，档案）
2003年——布什接待了俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京。
2012 年——巴拉克·奥巴马主持八国集团峰会。
左起，意大利总理马里奥·蒙蒂、英国首相戴维·卡梅伦、德国总理安格拉·默克尔和法国总统弗朗索瓦·奥朗德（右）聆听巴拉克·奥巴马总统在 2012 年 5 月 19 日星期六在马里兰州戴维营举行的八国集团峰会上的讲话（美联社照片/查尔斯·达拉帕克，档案）
2015 年 — 奥巴马主办波斯湾国家峰会。
2019 年——喀布尔发生爆炸事件，造成包括一名美国士兵在内的 12 人死亡后，特朗普取消了周末在戴维营与塔利班和阿富汗领导人举行的秘密会议。———
美联社记者达琳·苏佩尔维尔 (Darlene Superville) 为这一时间线提供了档案报道。

item.title: 国际足联高级管理人员表示员工因因凡蒂诺的世界杯抛售计划而受到欺骗
item.description:
日内瓦（美联社）——国际足联首席运营官表示，其工作人员被主席因凡蒂诺的世界杯抛售计划所欺骗，并于周五建议该项目不得继续进行。
苏黎世高管凯文·拉穆拉尔（Kevin Lamourall）在向美联社发表的一份声明中邀请因凡蒂诺解雇他，该声明为国际足联老板将未来世界杯利润股份出售给私募股权基金的计划带来的强烈影响为他的同事们辩护。
拉莫尔写道，工作人员因因凡蒂诺近几个月来在出售计划中缺乏开放性而“欺骗”了他们，“他们应该得到比蔑视和恐吓更好的待遇”。
“这是一个人的项目，”因凡蒂诺在国际足联和欧洲足球机构欧足联的长期同事拉莫尔写道。“这个项目不仅不能继续进行……而且现在是足球政治领导人问自己正确问题并做出正确决定的时候了。”
拉莫尔发表声明的几个小时前，因凡蒂诺的高级顾问卡洛斯·科代罗（Carlos Cordeiro）辞职并敦促国际足联其他高级工作人员发表讲话。卡洛斯·科代罗是前高盛银行家，代表足球机构参加世界杯世界杯工作组。
“当国际足联考虑出售世界杯股份时，我不能袖手旁观，”科代罗在一份声明中写道。这位前美国足协主席表示，他没有参与约书亚·库什纳创建的纽约投资基金支持的计划的谈判。
“让我澄清一下。我没有参与这项提议，并且我明确反对它，”科代罗说。他称这笔价值 200 亿美元的商业子公司“对足球界来说是一笔糟糕的交易”。
拉穆尔并未辞去自 2024 年以来一直担任的职务，但表示他对同事负有责任。
这位法国官员表示：“如果这意味着我会失去工作，那就这样吧。”“我会理解并尊重这个决定。至少今晚我会睡个好觉。”
二十年前，拉莫尔作为时任欧足联主席米歇尔·普拉蒂尼的助手从政界进入足球界。他经常在足球政治中发挥国际作用，与非洲和亚洲的国际足联成员联合会联络，这些联合会正在权衡自己对因凡蒂诺在 9 月 19 日截止日期前提出的各 2000 万美元报价的决定。
近年来，科代罗经常与因凡蒂诺一起进行工作访问，在白宫会见美国总统唐纳德·特朗普。
“足球一直是我生活的核心，在银行业工作超过 35 年之后，我既了解这项资产的价值，也了解放弃部分资产的后果，”他说。“这就是为什么这个提议应该被拒绝。”
欧洲国家已同意抵制世界杯和国际足联所有其他赛事，以抗议詹尼·因凡蒂诺将私募股权投资者引入足球界最大赛事的计划。北美足球机构也拒绝了这一提议。这是您需要了解的内容。
因凡蒂诺提议将国际足联的商业业务（包括男子和女子世界杯和世俱杯）分拆为一家价值 200 亿美元的子公司，其中 20% 的股份由私人投资者持有。国际足联描述的“主要投资者”是库什纳，他是特朗普女婿贾里德·库什纳的弟弟。
“国际足联已经获得了非凡的财政资源。该组织拥有数十亿美元的储备，并且没有债务，”科代罗说。他指出，国际足联在过去四年中与刚刚结束的男子世界杯相关的收入为 150 亿美元。
“在这种背景下，出售足球最有价值资产的永久股份来筹集 42 亿美元毫无意义。这是在没有任何令人信服的理由的情况下抵押足球的未来，”他说。
科代罗表示，他与因凡蒂诺一起为国际足联工作了五年，与“敬业、有原则、深切关心这项运动的人”一起工作。
“我希望他们也能大声疾呼，”他写道，“因为如此重大的决定应该是为了足球的利益，而不是那些从中获利的人的利益。”
因凡蒂诺担任国际足联主席已经十多年了，明年三月他似乎肯定会在无人反对的情况下连任。国际足联设定了 11 月 18 日为挑战者挺身而出的最后期限。
拉穆尔是因凡蒂诺核心圈子的一员，他们为他竞选2016年2月的国际足联主席选举出人意料地获胜。

item.title: 因凡蒂诺在遭到巨大阻力后放弃了将世界杯利润出售给私募股权的计划
item.description:
日内瓦（美联社）——在遭到足球界各个角落的抵制后，国际足联主席詹尼·因凡蒂诺放弃了将世界杯利润出售给私人股本的分裂计划。
因凡蒂诺的决定是在他担任白宫小组成员的高级顾问辞职、亚洲足球机构与欧洲和北美一起反对这一决定后作出的。
因凡蒂诺在周六早些时候的一份声明中表示：“在仔细听取了所有意见后，很明显，该项目已经造成了某种性质的分歧，无论支持程度如何，都不再符合最初设定的目标。”“我们的目的一直是——也将永远是——团结和进步。因此，这个提案不会继续下去。”
因凡蒂诺曾提议创建一家价值 200 亿美元的公司，与包括库什纳家族在内的私人投资者一起运营世界杯，但自周二宣布这一消息以来，遭到了日益强烈的反对。

“这是一个人的项目，”因凡蒂诺在国际足联和欧洲足球机构欧足联的长期同事拉穆尔写道。“这个项目不仅不能继续进行……而且现在是足球政治领导人问自己正确问题并做出正确决定的时候了。”
因凡蒂诺提议将国际足联的商业业务（包括男子和女子世界杯和世俱杯）分拆为一家价值 200 亿美元的子公司，其中 20% 的股份由私人投资者持有。
国际足联描述的“主要投资者”是一家总部位于纽约的投资公司，由美国总统唐纳德·特朗普的女婿贾里德·库什纳的弟弟约书亚·库什纳创建。
国际足联的下一场比赛是 9 月 5 日在波兰举行的 20 岁以下女子世界杯，欧足联成员表示他们将抵制该赛事。
这一失误可能会让因凡蒂诺付出高昂的代价，特别是在拉莫尔和科代罗介入之后。
因凡蒂诺在 2019 年和 2023 年均无异议连任，根据国际足联法规，他可以再连任四年。下届主席竞选的最后期限是 11 月 18 日，距离国际足联非洲总部所在地摩洛哥拉巴特投票整整四个月。
尽管人们长期以来对因凡蒂诺的风格感到不安，而且之前曾试图强行通过不受欢迎的项目，但因凡蒂诺的职位似乎已经稳固，但由于私募股权提案的失败，他的职位可能会变得更加脆弱。

item.title: 巨人队在摩托车事故后暂停向受伤的外野手哈里森·巴德支付工资
item.description:
圣地亚哥（美联社）——旧金山巨人队暂停向受伤的外野手哈里森·巴德支付费用，因为他在上周末的一次摩托车事故中左脚受伤加重。
巴德自五月底以来一直因左脚足底筋膜炎缺席。该团队表示，周日凌晨在旧金山发生事故后，伤势更加严重。
巨人队棒球运营总裁巴斯特·波西周五在一份声明中表示：“周末，哈里森·巴德遭遇了一场事故，这导致哈里森之前的足底筋膜炎治疗时间表被推迟，不幸的是，他也无法重返赛场。”“我们仍在调查事故情况，但将暂停向哈里森付款，直到他能够恢复为俱乐部提供服务。”
巴德在本赛季之前与巨人队签订了一份为期两年、价值2050万美元的合同，其中包括本赛季450万美元的底薪。他在本赛季余下的比赛中被欠142万美元。
据《旧金山纪事报》报道，周日凌晨 2 点左右，巴德在旧金山滨海区骑摩托车时发生车祸。他被送往医院，没有生命危险。
32 岁的巴德在 30 场比赛中击球率为 0.170，打出 5 个本垒打，打点 14 个，OPS 为 0.557，之后才进入伤病名单。
这并不是巴德第一次在摩托车事故中陷入困境。据《盖恩斯维尔太阳报》报道，2014 年，他在佛罗里达州读大学时，因驾驶电动滑板车撞上路边撞上一辆卡车而被停学。根据引用的事件报告，他躺在地上没有反应，身上有酒精味。

item.title: FCC 主席为针对 ABC 的行动辩护，称广播公司必须“为了公共利益”运营
item.description:
联邦通信委员会主席布伦丹·卡尔周五为其机构最近针对美国广播公司的行动进行了辩护，称广播公司有责任“以公共利益为重”，而联邦通信委员会只是试图恢复这一标准。
卡尔在接受福克斯商业网络采访时表示，像美国广播公司这样的广播公司“与美国人民达成了一项协议。你们广播公司可以获得补贴，可以免费使用宝贵的公共资源，即价值数十亿美元的电视广播。作为交换，你们必须以公共利益为重。”
卡尔告诉主播玛丽亚·巴蒂罗莫：“看，作为一个国家，我们应该拥有一个值得信赖、受人尊敬的新闻媒体，但我们还没有做到这一点。”“所以我希望更多的广播公司回归到他们的公共利益义务。”
此前一天，美国广播公司在与唐纳德·特朗普总统的联邦通信委员会的不断升级的斗争中再次发起猛攻，再次指责该机构公然试图压制其受宪法保护的言论自由，进而压制美国所有媒体的言论自由。
ABC 指责该机构对其进行报复仅仅是因为它不喜欢 ABC 节目的政治内容。
该网络在向该机构提交的最新文件中发表了新评论，正式反对 FCC 于 4 月份启动的对 ABC 八个本地广播许可证到期前的早期审查。
文件称：“毫无疑问，委员会为什么要挑选这八个电台。”“每个节目都属于 ABC 旗下，政府多次公开呼吁撤销 ABC 的许可证，因为它不喜欢 ABC 网络节目所表达的内容和观点。”
“对美国广播公司的报复向该国每家媒体公司发出了一个信号，”它继续说道。“适应政府对新闻报道应该是什么样子的看法，否则就要付出代价……工具各不相同，但目标却没有变化：媒体行业太害怕官方报复而不敢自由报道新闻。”
许可证审查只是美国广播公司和美国联邦通信委员会之间长期对抗的一部分。该电视台还在与卡尔制作《The View》的努力作斗争，这是一档脱口秀节目，其主持人和嘉宾经常激怒特朗普，并遵守平等时间规则——ABC 表示，该机构本身在二十多年前就已经解决了这个问题。
这些规则要求给予竞争公职的候选人平等的通话时间。真正的新闻节目除外。FCC 在 2002 年的一项决定中认定该节目具有此类资格。
特朗普还多次呼吁解雇深夜主持人吉米·金梅尔。
当美国联邦通信委员会 (FCC) 在 4 月份对美国广播公司 (ABC) 的牌照进行早期审查时，正值美国联邦通信委员会 (FCC) 因一个冒犯特朗普的笑话而与金梅尔发生争执。然而，该机构引用了该公司的多元化、公平性和包容性做法，卡尔在福克斯采访中也提到了这些做法。
他说，为了公共利益行事，“意味着你不能歪曲新闻、广播恶作剧。你不能参与这种令人反感的 DEI 歧视形式。”他没有详细说明。
ABC 在周四提交的文件中提到了 FCC 网站上发布的超过 14 万条评论，其中超过 95% 的评论支持 ABC 的立场。
“对于许可证更新程序来说，对电视台的大量支持是前所未有的，”它说。“这些支持者跨越了意识形态范围，但都对言论自由和新闻自由有着共同的基本承诺。”
美国广播公司在其冗长的文件中还指出，联邦通信委员会要求提前申请许可证更新的情况是多么罕见。
美国广播公司表示，“直到委员会采取这一步骤的前一天，它已经有五十多年没有要求提前申请许可证续签了。”“委员会背离这些规范的行为暴露了真实情况：政府正在对美国广播公司行使其第一修正案权利进行报复。
“仅凭这一点就应该阻止这些诉讼程序的进行。”
乔斯林·诺维克 (Jocelyn Noveck) 为美联社报道媒体和娱乐的交叉领域。

item.title: 监管机构提议对银行如何向中低收入社区提供贷款的法律进行全面改革
item.description:
纽约（美联社）——特朗普政府宣布对民权时代一项重要立法的规则进行全面改革，最引人注目的是减少需要完全遵守法律的银行数量。
美国货币监理署和联邦存款保险公司周五联合宣布了对《社区再投资法》的拟议修改，该法要求监管机构记录银行向中低收入社区提供贷款的情况。这将是近三十年来对该法律规则和规定的首次重大修订。
根据拟议的修订，银行审查员将更加重视银行在某些社区和地区提供的贷款，而不是银行开设的分支机构数量或从当地社区吸收的存款数量。
需要遵守该法律的银行数量也将减少。小型银行的定义将从资产低于4.12亿美元的银行扩大到资产为10亿美元的银行。资产在 10 亿美元至 100 亿美元之间的银行现在将被归类为中间银行。
这将使需要遵守 CRA 部分规定的银行数量减少 800 家。根据新规定，只有 86 家银行（约占所有机构的 3%）将受到 CRA 的全面监管。
另一个可能引起争议的变化涉及银行如何向社区发展团体提供资金。根据 CRA，银行可以向在其社区从事贫困或低收入住房工作的当地组织捐款，以表明他们正在向当地社区提供资源。新规定可能会缩小银行为履行这些义务而可以捐赠的团体和项目。
银行监管机构在总结变化时表示，这些变化将确保社区发展拨款“不会被转用于激进主义事业或因过高的运营成本而消耗”。银行还需要收集有关谁获得社区补助金的更详细信息，包括地址，这将使谁从银行获得补助金更加透明。
这一变化可能会对全国社区再投资联盟等团体产生负面影响，该联盟是社区发展团体的伞式团体，经常从 CRA 下的银行获得资金。新规定不鼓励银行向国家组织提供赠款，而是将赠款集中于地方团体。
NCRC 首席执行官 Jesse Van Tol 表示，银行监管机构将 CRA 下的拨款政治化是“不幸的”。
“CRA 的创建是为了为中低收入人群服务。其中许多变化将阻止银行发放赠款，特别是在农村地区，我预计那里的活动将会大幅下降，”Van Tol 说。
OCC 和 FDIC 周五宣布的提案不包括另一家主要银行监管机构——美联储。银行集团一直在推动所有三个监管机构提出联合提案，以确保这三个机构都符合 CRA 的相同要求。
CRA 于 1977 年通过，旨在打击红线，即银行选择不在少数族裔占多数的社区或贫困社区放贷或开设分行，从而歧视穷人和少数族裔。
该法律很复杂，要求银行记录其在经营所在城市和地区开展业务的情况。银行必须接受定期检查，以了解其是否遵守法律。不良的 CRA 检查可能会限制银行开设新分行或与另一家银行合并的能力，或产生其他后果。司法部也将通过 CRA 收集的数据用于红线案件。
CRA 法规的最后一次重大修订发生在 1995 年，双方政府多次尝试更新规则，以反映银行和金融服务在过去 30 年中的变化。但这些修改一再失败，要么是由于其他监管机构、银行或社区团体的反对，要么是被法院阻止。拜登政府尝试自行修改 CRA 规则，但这些修改被德克萨斯州法院阻止。
拟议的规则现在将进入为期 60 天的征求意见期，待银行、社区团体和其他各方有机会对这些变化进行权衡后最终确定。

item.title: 一枚废弃的 SpaceX 火箭正在与月球高速碰撞
item.description:
佛罗里达州卡纳维拉尔角（美联社）——一年多前发射了一对月球着陆器后，一枚漂浮的 SpaceX 火箭正在与月球相撞。
火箭的上级将于周三无意中撞向月球，在月球上留下一个陨石坑，并扬起一缕灰尘和碎石，科学家和天文爱好者都渴望观察到这一点。
太空追踪专家比尔·格雷预测，月球阳光照射下的西缘爱因斯坦陨石坑附近会发生 5,400 英里/小时（8,700 公里/小时）的撞击，是音速的七倍。由于活动在凌晨进行，美国东部和加拿大以及南美大部分地区应该能看到最好的景色。
虽然科学家们并不太关心这块特殊的太空垃圾，但它凸显了随着越来越多的物体挤入轨道，威胁日益严重。
“那里的情况变得越来越拥挤，”格雷说，他计划从加拿大新不伦瑞克省查看后果。
SpaceX 从来没有打算登陆月球。但太空专家表示，如果上级被推入绕太阳轨道，坠机事件是可以避免的。
这将是已知的第二枚因意外坠入月球而死亡的火箭。2022年，中国的一枚火箭在月球背面挖出了一对陨石坑。
对于天文学家来说幸运的是，即将到来的撞击将发生在月球近侧，其能量相当于三吨 TNT 炸药。
专家表示，撞击闪光持续时间不到一秒，可能会因为太暗而无法看到。但喷射出的物质流可能会延伸到太空几英里（公里），并且望远镜可以看到数十分钟。
洛斯阿拉莫斯国家实验室的本杰明·费尔南多说：“月球上的重力很低，没有风可以吹走灰尘。”他鼓励专业人士和业余爱好者进行观测。
他在一封电子邮件中补充道：“我们对这一事件感兴趣的部分原因是想弄清楚碎片撞击对未来宇航员造成了多大的危害。”
费尔南多预计撞击坑宽近 90 英尺，深 16 英尺（宽 27 米，深 5 米），太小，从地球上看不到，但航天器可以看到。
美国宇航局的月球勘测轨道飞行器和韩国的 Danuri 月球轨道飞行器将收集坠机现场前后的照片。费尔南多和他的团队表示，在撞击前两分钟，达努里将偏离 SpaceX 火箭一两英里（几公里）的范围。
废弃的火箭部分长约 40 英尺（12 米），重约 10,000 磅（4,500 公斤），于 2025 年 1 月 15 日吊起了两架私人月球着陆器。
其中之一——萤火虫航空航天公司的“蓝色幽灵”——成为第一艘完全成功着陆月球的私人航天器。另一个是日本 ispace 的着陆器失事。
科学家们表示，由于流星体和其他自然物体在撞击月球之前几乎不会发出任何警告，因此通过观察像即将出现的人造物体那样的精心跟踪的撞击，可以学到很多东西。美国宇航局在阿波罗时代将火箭部件和登月舱扔进月球进行地震测量。几十年后的 2009 年，NASA 故意使 LCROSS 航天器和上部级坠毁，以在月球南极附近寻找冰。
科学家表示，随着月球成为新的旅行热点，在机器人和宇航员抵达之前改善碎片监测和交通控制至关重要。
美国和中国正在竞相在未来几年内将宇航员送上月球。埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 的 SpaceX 和杰夫·贝佐斯 (Jeff Bezos) 的蓝色起源 (Blue Origin) 正在争夺为 NASA 尚未命名的阿耳忒弥斯 IV 号月球漫步者提供着陆器，后者将接替 12 名阿波罗宇航员在月球表面漫步。
“这种影响不会成为问题，”退休天体物理学家乔纳森·麦克道尔在一封电子邮件中说。“但在未来，如果月球上有长期基地，类似的影响将成为一个问题，我们不需要将火箭级留在这种混乱的轨道上。”
美联社健康与科学部得到霍华德休斯医学院科学教育部和罗伯特伍德约翰逊基金会的支持。美联社对所有内容全权负责。

item.title: 事实焦点：移民在西班牙休达过境引发未经证实的说法
item.description:
BARCELONA, Spain (AP) — Acrisis at the border in Ceuta, a tiny Spanish territory in North Africa, has resulted in unsubstantiated claims about Spain’s migration policies and the causes of the border surge at the territory’s frontier with Morocco.
Some60,000 migrants entered Ceutafrom Morocco on Thursday and Friday, local Spanish officials have said, equivalent to 70% of the city’s regular population. At least 57 migrants died attempting the crossing either by drowning while trying to swim to Spanish territory or in a stampede.
CLAIM: Spain’s move to legalize the status of immigrants caused the rush.
THE FACTS: Spain’s government is carrying out anamnesty for immigrantswithout residency permits who could prove they had been living in the country for at least five months and arrived before Jan. 1, 2026. Over1 million people appliedbefore the window closed at the end of last month.
Critics, including U.S. President Donald Trump and his administration, say that the amnesty sparked the rush to the Ceuta border by sending the message that Spain is lenient on migrants.
Spain’s “weak law, bad management” was to blame, Trump said Friday. The U.S. State Department doubled down in a post on X, saying that “this unacceptable incident is the direct result of the Spanish Government’s deliberate efforts to enable and facilitate mass illegal migration into Europe.”
Spain’s government strongly rejects that premise, saying that criminal gangs were behind the border crisis. Madrid has tried to maintain a hard line on illegal attempts to cross its borders while encouraging orderly arrivals of workers, who the government says are needed to keep up the country’s strong economy.
Poverty and youth unemployment are high in neighboring Morocco, particularly away from coastal cities that have experienced some development in recent years.Gen Z-led protestslast year called for social justice and better public services. The inequality has prompted many young Moroccans to attempt to leave for Europe in search of better economic opportunities.
Still, it isn’t fully clear what caused the sudden surge in crossings at Ceuta.
CLAIM: A misconstrued Spanish court ruling is to blame.
THE FACTS: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez has pushed the argument that a recent ruling by Spain’s Supreme Court had been intentionally misconstrued by migrant smugglers to convince thousands of people to cross the border by swimming around the border fence.
That court ruling said migrants arriving by sea could not be summarily deported without due process, unlike those who cross by land or climb the border fence because they had not crossed a physical barrier.
Migration and human rights activists said social media posts and misinformation helped fuel the departures.
“The departures were promoted in a certain way. At first, people were hearing that the border was open, and then everyone started referring to the Spanish court decision. That contributed to the crossings,” said Achraf Maimouni, a human-rights activist.
CLAIM: Morocco intentionally opened the border
THE FACTS: In 2021, more than8,000 people crossed the Ceuta borderwhen Moroccan border officials dropped their guard, sparking a diplomatic crisis between the neighbors.
The move was broadly interpreted as retaliation from Morocco for Spain’s decision to allow a pro-independence leader from the disputedWestern Sahara regionto receive medical treatment at a Spanish hospital. Sánchez defused the crisis when he shiftedhis country’s long-standing position on Western Sahara, andmet with Moroccan King Mohammed VIthe following year.
In this most recent crisis, which dwarfs the one five years prior, the first response by Spanish officials was to say that Moroccan counterparts were working alongside them to stop the rush. Whatever those efforts were, they proved ineffective as migrants kept steadily coming from all over Morocco to the border, with thousands breaching the frontier on Thursday and Friday.
An Associated Press freelance photographer witnessed Moroccan gendarmes standing aside with their arms crossed on Thursday as thousands of migrants passed near them into Ceuta. Eventually, Moroccan security forces stepped up, employing tear gas, batons and water cannons to disperse large groups of migrants reaching the border on Friday.
Morocco’s ambassador to Spain expressed hope that those who crossed from Morocco into the Spanish territory would return, saying the situation had unfolded against Rabat’s wishes.
Yet Morocco has never officially recognized Ceuta and its sister Spanish enclave, Melilla, as European territories even though they have beenunder Spanish control for centuries.
CLAIM: The surge in migrants is payback for Sánchez’ position on Iran and Gaza.
The mass crossing has given birth to conspiracy theories online, including one take that sees Trump and Israel encouraging a friendly Morocco to let this happen as payback for Spain’s position on immigration and its harsh criticism of their joint attack on Iran and the Israeli military campaign in Gaza.
THE FACTS: Trump has for months raged against Spain and recently threatened to end trade with the European country, and the Israeli leader has accused Spain of waging a diplomatic war against his country. But there is no evidence to support claims of a U.S. or Israeli hand in the Ceuta crisis.
CLAIM: Those who crossed will end up in mainland Europe.
THE FACTS: The Ceuta crossings have led to political leaders in Italy, France and other EU nations to take measures that appear aimed at stopping people from entering their countries. Premier Giorgia Meloni threatened to suspend Italy’s open-border Schengen agreement with Spain even though Italy doesn’t share a border with Spain and receives many more migrants crossing the Mediterranean than Spain. French Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said France would also strengthen border checks with Spain.
While the influx is clearly unmanageable for the city of Ceuta, the impact of the crossing will mostly be limited to the Spanish territory and have limited impact on mainland Spain.
By Friday evening, the majority of migrants had already returned to Morocco voluntarily, Spanish authorities said. Those who remain in Ceuta will either be sent back eventually or face a long period of legal limbo and possibly spells in government-run centers.
EU migration commissioner Magnus Brunner posted on X that “not a single person has crossed to mainland EU” and that the Schengen Borders Code already includes special border checks for people traveling from Ceuta and Melilla.
